newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Seven charged in Portugal disco fire case.
newsitem.headline: Seven charged in Portugal disco fire case.

text.p: Portuguese police have arrested seven people suspected of starting a fire in a discotheque which killed 13 people and was the country's most violent crime in living memory.

Police chief Fernando Negrao told a news conference on Sunday that seven suspects had been charged in connection with the fire at the Meia Culpa discotheque in the northern town of Amarante on April 16. Five would remain in prison pending trial.
Thirteen people died and 13 were injured after masked men burst into the club and doused the walls and furniture in petrol before setting them alight.
Negrao said that one of the suspects being held was the owner of a rival discotheque.
"At this stage it looks as if the basic motive for the crime was commercial rivalry between these types of establishment," he said.
The Portuguese media has reported that both the 'Meia Culpa' and its local rival, 'The Black Diamond', were clubs where prostitutes met their clients.
But Negrao ruled out media speculation that an organised drug or prostitution ring was behind the attack.
"There is nothing that points to any links with organised crime. This was an isolated event," he said.
